Maia for Incident handoffs

Hand off the incident without losing the facts.

Maia turns the current timeline and responder notes into a structured handoff. The incoming responder sees what is known, what changed, and what remains open.

All use cases ↗

Capture the current state

An incident handoff should help the next responder act without rereading every message. Start with the approved timeline, current symptoms, mitigation status, relevant dashboards or records, and the outgoing responder's open questions.

Ask Maia to label facts, hypotheses, and planned checks separately. This prevents a theory repeated in the channel from becoming an accepted cause.

Prepare the handoff

Maia can order events by timestamp, identify the latest confirmed mitigation, and list owners for active checks. It can link each statement to the supplied incident record or thread message.

The packet should also state what was not checked. Missing evidence matters when a responder chooses the next investigation path.

Include the last known customer impact and the timestamp of that observation. If impact is still changing, say so. Do not copy an early estimate into the handoff as though it remains current.

Review it in the incident thread

The outgoing responder reviews the draft where the incident team can see it. Teammates can correct a timestamp or mark an experiment complete. The incoming responder acknowledges ownership and asks follow-up questions in the same thread.

Maia helps maintain the record. It does not autonomously remediate systems or guarantee that the service has recovered.

A practical example

An API error spike began at 14:06. A cache configuration changed at 14:19, and errors fell by 14:24. The team suspects a delayed-job backlog but has not confirmed it. Maia writes those events in order, links the evidence, and lists the queue check as the next action.

The outgoing responder corrects one timestamp and adds the relevant dashboard. The incoming responder accepts the handoff with a clear starting point.

Improve the next handoff

Give the incident channel a standard format with service, impact, current state, actions taken, open hypotheses, next checks, and owners. A stable format helps Maia find gaps without inventing detail.

Keep the handoff short enough to scan during an active incident. Link to detailed logs and dashboards rather than pasting large outputs into the thread. The incoming responder should identify the first action and main unknown within a minute.

Common questions

Can Maia determine the root cause?

It can organize evidence and compare hypotheses. An engineer must confirm the cause through investigation.

Does Maia monitor the service?

Only if a verified connection supplies that data. Otherwise, use approved snapshots or exports and state their timestamps.

Can Maia update the incident record?

It can draft an update. A verified write should follow the incident team's approval policy.
